children: PwC plans to reduce bonuses for some employees in Switzerland by about 50% as the accounting and consulting firm responds to a difficult economy, changing client demand and the growing use of artificial intelligence, Bloomberg News reported Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Employees learned of the reductions during recent meetings with individual teams, the people said. PwC Switzerland declined to comment on internal personnel decisions or confirm the reported cuts.
The company reportedly told staff that layoffs were not under consideration at this time.

The reported bonus cuts offer another sign that AI is changing the economics of professional services. Automation may eventually increase productivity and profit margins, but firms first must contend with weaker demand, excess staffing and pressure from clients to pay less for work that technology can perform faster. For investors in consulting firms, staffing companies and business-software providers, the shift could favor vendors that help companies automate operations while creating headwinds for labor-intensive service models.

PwC is not alone in reducing expenses. KPMG is cutting about 200 advisory jobs in Britain, while McKinsey, EY and PwC’s U.S. operation have eliminated support positions as firms expand their use of AI and outsourcing.

Switzerland had been an attractive market for major consultancies because of its concentration of multinational corporations, banks and pharmaceutical companies. That environment has become less favorable as clients reduce spending.

PwC recently lost Roche as a major account after the drugmaker curtailed its use of large consulting firms. The disappearance of Credit Suisse as an independent company also removed a significant prospective client after its acquisition by UBS.
